newsitem.title: MOROCCO: S. Korea Daewoo, Morocco finalise $28.7 mln accord.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea Daewoo, Morocco finalise $28.7 mln accord.

text.p: Morocco and South Korean giant conglomerate Daewoo, which plans to invest up to $900 million in Morocco, on Wednesday signed the final agreement to buy Rabat's five-star Hyatt Regency hotel.

"We are very glad that Daewoo signed today the final agreement of buying Hyatt Regency, one of Morocco's best hotels at $28.7 million," Khalid El-Kadiri, head of Caisse de Depot et de Gestion (CDG), told reporters.
The signing ceremony took place in presence of Daewoo representatives and Moroccan officials at the headquarters of state-run CDG in Rabat, former main shareholder in the hotel.

Daewoo is expected to invest an extra $10 million to renovate the hotel, Kadiri said. The group also agreed to spend another $40 million to extend the hotel facilities located in a residential area of the capital and close to the royal palace.
Daewoo earlier said it plans to invest up to $900 million in Morocco's productive sectors including telecommunications.

The Moroccan Trade Minister Driss Jettou who started earlier this week an official tour in South East Asia, is expected to visit Seoul to sign a second agreement with Daewoo for investment in the industrial sector, a Moroccan official said.
No other details were immediately available.
